title: Early life; university enrollment at 82; Ray Gibbs journalism class
description: Clara Grove introduces herself, born in 1879 on a farm near Van Meter, Iowa, and tells a childhood story about hiding in the family well. She describes enrolling at the University of Idaho at age 82 at her daughter's urging, taking classes for two years, joining Ray Gibbs's journalism class, selling a manuscript, and treating the class to coffee in the Student Union.

title: Hearing advice; changes to the Moscow campus
description: Clara advises how to speak clearly to people with poor hearing. She then describes how the University of Idaho campus has changed, recalling Morrow Hall, the Science Building, the Ad Building, the old Student Union, the ATO fraternity, and the Alpha Chi Omega and Tri-Delt houses.

title: University coursework; Ray Gibbs as a teacher
description: Clara discusses the journalism course she took and the dean who helped her enroll. She praises Ray Gibbs as an outstanding teacher who stayed in control of his class and blamed himself when only one manuscript sold.

title: Work in Moscow; nursing; cooking for sororities; teaching
description: Clara recounts her work in Moscow, including a brief stint at a newspaper office, nursing at Moscow Hospital and in Colfax, private nursing, and cooking for sororities in Moscow and Pullman. She then describes her seven years teaching country schools, including a year in Darneil, Montana, and tells a story about students reciting road-show rhymes.

title: Coping with discouragement; owning the Troy News; daughter's education and family life
description: Clara explains how a Denver doctor's advice to 'just keep going' helped her through low periods, including a recent week-long 'recession.' She recounts buying the Troy News from Wilbert Johns, hand-setting type, running an old press, and putting out a supplement, then describes her determination to send her daughter Ethel to university and her son-in-law Lawrence's engineering career and retirement home near the Mojave Desert.

title: Politics and public figures; presidents; MacArthur; crowds
description: Clara names Teddy Roosevelt as a favorite president and shares anecdotes about General MacArthur, a crushing crowd at a New Jersey basketball game, and the disputed death of a president rumored to have committed suicide.

title: Hard times in Dakota; women's movement; Dear Abby
description: Clara recalls hard times in Dakota Territory, her mother feeding hungry travelers, and housing student couples in Moscow. She gives her views on the women's movement, modern dress, and answers from the Dear Abby advice column.

title: Marriage and widowhood
description: Clara briefly answers questions about her marriage, which began in 1907 and ended with her husband's death many years ago.

title: Marriage, tact and lost formality; life with grandparents; work ethic on the South Dakota plains; threshing and lean crops; hauling water and digging a well
description: Clara Grove declines to discuss her unhappy marriage but expounds on tact and the lost formality of earlier times. She recalls living with her grandparents on the South Dakota plains, the relentless work expected of her as a girl, the grandmother's rigid routines, threshing wheat on Uncle Will's farm in a year of poor yields, and the scarcity of water, including hauling it in barrels and the success of the well her sister insisted be dug.

title: Closing; scheduling the next session
description: Isabel Miller suggests stopping, and Clara thanks the class, encouraging them to prepare questions for next time. They agree to meet again in two weeks at five o'clock, and Clara mentions her ten years running the Good Will. Isabel offers to drive her home.
